text:
nina: FYI — Escalation from Paywise. They see tool results getting attached to the wrong tool when they fan out parallel tool calls. Happens intermittently under load, causes wrong data to be returned and schema validation mismatches on our side. Customer provided a repro and logs. Can eng take a look?

ryan: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and any correlation_id / request ids from logs? Suspect correlation mapping but want concrete traces.

nina: Pasting condensed logs and the client's parallel call payload. Notice repeated call_id in log lines.

nina: ```
# client request (trimmed)
POST /v1/generate
{
  "input": "...",
  "tools": ["extract_entities","lookup_db","format_output"],
  "fanout_parallel": true,
  "call_id": "paywise-req-42"  # client-level id only
}

# server logs (race window)
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 tool=extract_entities started
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 tool=lookup_db started
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 tool=extract_entities finished result_id=toolres-7
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 tool=format_output started
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 tool=lookup_db finished result_id=toolres-3
[2026-12-04T15:03:12Z] request_id=paywise-req-42 mapping: toolres-3 -> extract_entities  <-- wrong mapping
```

nina: Customer reports that the schema validator in the application saw a shape that belonged to lookup_db but it was used as extract_entities output, so downstream crashes.

leo: Looks like we only use the top-level call_id to correlate sub-tool results back to the parent. If client doesn't attach a unique per-subcall id, our fanout code relies on an internal ephemeral token that can collide when handling many parallel callbacks — especially with our current non-atomic mapping write.

ryan: Can you share a repro script? if we can reproduce locally we can iterate quickly.

sophia: (from Paywise) repro attached: small Node snippet they run with Promise.all — they don't set per-tool call id. Happens ~1/50 runs under load.

sophia: ```js
// simplified repro (client side)
const tools = ['extract_entities','lookup_db','format_output']
await Promise.all(tools.map(t => fetch('/v1/tool_call', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ tool: t, call_id: 'paywise-req-42' })
})))
```

ryan: OK repro confirmed locally. I can reproduce wrong associations by hammering Promise.all with concurrency 30. The root cause: our correlation map uses call_id as the key and writes a mapping entry for each returning tool without a unique subcall key, and writes are racy (no per-call lock or atomic append).

leo: Quick mitigation: treat the fanout each subcall as call_id + subcall_index when creating map keys. We can also require clients to supply a unique tool_call_id per subcall and fall back to an auto-generated UUID server-side if missing.

ryan: Proposed hotfix: change mapping from map[call_id] = lastSeenResult to map[call_id].results[sub_index] = result. Also switch updates to use atomic compare-and-swap (in our runtime map abstraction). Small patch ready in branch fix/tool-fanout-assoc-2026. Patch excerpt:```diff
- correlationMap.set(callId, { last: result })
+ const bucket = correlationMap.get(callId) || { results: {} }
+ bucket.results[subIndex] = result
+ correlationMap.set(callId, bucket)
```

ryan: I'll open the PR and run unit + load tests. Planning a canary deploy to dev then prod if green.

nina: For immediate customer mitigation can we force-sequential fanout for Paywise route? That should avoid races while we patch.

leo: Yes — we can update route config to set fanout.parallel=false for customer:paywise. Command: `redwood routes update paywise --set fanout.parallel=false` — I can run that and confirm.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-134 created for Paywise — priority P1, owner ryan.

ryan: I'll run load test against canary in ~30m. If results stable, we can ship to prod and notify Paywise with rollback window.

nina: Thanks. After patch we should add an integration test that simulates high-concurrency Promise.all style fanout and asserts no result mis-association. Also add monitoring alert when schema validation errors spike for any customer.

sophia: Thanks team — Paywise appreciates the quick mitigation. Please keep us posted on ETA.

ryan: ETA: PR opened in 2 hours, canary in 6 hours, full rollout in 12-24h pending load test. I'll update thread and tag you. :thumbsup:
